extracted.intended_audience: California state agency staff, regulated entities, and members of the public who participate in or submit materials for California rulemaking under the Administrative Procedure Act
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and procedural standards for preparing, submitting, and publishing administrative regulations under the California Administrative Procedure Act, and for public participation in that rulemaking process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory review standards
rubrics_metrics.description: OAL ensures that agency regulations are clear, necessary, legally valid, and available to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OAL reviews administrative regulations proposed by over 200 state agencies for compliance with statutory standards, and is responsible for transmitting approved regulations to the Secretary of State and publishing them in the California Code of Regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with the California Administrative Procedure Act (APA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed regulations must comply with the standards set forth in California’s Administrative Procedure Act (APA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OAL reviews proposed regulations for APA compliance as part of its authority; compliance encompasses the substantive and procedural requirements the APA imposes (the page links to further resources and the APA booklet).

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmission and publication requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: OAL transmits regulations to the Secretary of State and publishes regulations in the California Code of Regulations (CCR).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must follow OAL procedures for transmitting rulemaking actions so that regulations can be properly filed and published in the official CCR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory electronic submission of actions to OAL
rubrics_metrics.description: Beginning April 1, 2026, all actions submitted electronically to OAL must be submitted using OAL’s eSubmissions Portal; submissions via email will not be accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OAL has created a dedicated eSubmissions webpage with instructional videos, FAQs, and related materials; agencies should use the portal for all submissions after the effective date and may contact the Reference Attorney for questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 101 certification, digital signatures, and electronic submission requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: OAL's frequently asked questions address the Section 101 certification, use of digital signatures, and requirements for electronic submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies and filers must ensure their electronic filings satisfy Section 101 certification and digital signature requirements per OAL guidance; see OAL's FAQs and instructional materials on the eSubmissions Portal for specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation by reference standards for CCR
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on how to incorporate a document by reference into the California Code of Regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OAL provides a short instructional video titled 'How to Incorporate a Document by Reference in the California Code of Regulations' to assist agencies with proper incorporation procedures and requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commenting on emergency rulemaking actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures and guidance for members of the public on how to comment on emergency rulemaking actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OAL offers resources including a short video 'How to Comment on Emergency Rulemaking Actions' and other training materials to help the public understand how to participate in emergency rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Underground regulation identification and training
rubrics_metrics.description: OAL offers training and resources on underground regulations and provides oversight to address underground regulatory actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OAL advertises a Special 3-Hour Training for State Agency Personnel on Underground Regulations taught by experienced OAL attorneys; the training aims to identify and prevent underground regulations and to instruct agency staff on compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and notice procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: OAL makes proposed regulations and notices available to the public and provides mechanisms to receive notice of proposed rulemakings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members of the public can sign up for OAL's mailing list (oalproposedrulemakings@oal.ca.gov) to receive notice of proposed rulemakings; OAL publishes the California Regulatory Notice Register and the CCR to ensure public availability.
